disease_label_per_paper: Varicella zoster aseptic meningitis in an immunocompetent adult without typical rash
presentation_summary: 29-year-old previously healthy immunocompetent woman presented with five days of headache, photophobia, chills, and mild neck stiffness.
She had mild diarrhea before the headache and household children with diarrhea and mild fever before her illness.
She had no reported fever, paresthesia, or hearing loss at presentation; neurologic examination and cranial nerves were normal.
Exam showed a small right gluteal erythematous vesicular lesion that was not dermatomal and was initially considered an insect bite rather than typical zoster.
CBC showed WBC 7.8 K/uL and inflammatory markers were normal.
CSF showed WBC 454 cells/uL and protein 157 mg/dL; VZV was detected by CSF PCR and bacterial antigen testing was negative.
She received two days of IV acyclovir, then completed high-dose oral valacyclovir because she declined prolonged hospitalization.
At day 10 after discharge she developed recurrent headache and decreased right-ear hearing; repeat CSF was normal and VZV PCR was negative, with subsequent partial hearing recovery.
